procedure.label: Reported or filed
procedure.guidance: Keep the acknowledgement if you have one. Note where and when you reported or filed the matter, and ask that office how to check its status.

evidence_plan.heading: Scene and evidence review
evidence_plan.safety: Get to safety and seek medical or police help if needed. Do not enter or alter a scene to gather evidence. Leave physical collection to the authorities.
prompts: Where did each event happen, and what was the last confirmed time before it?
What did you actually see or hear? Where were you, and what could you see from there?
What was already different when you arrived, and what changed afterward? Say if you are unsure.
scene_points: The complainant, Deepak Rawat, says Imran punched him in the face and smashed his phone on the pavement during an argument over a parking spot.

suggestions.title: Report and acknowledgements
suggestions.look_for: Find the date, office or officer, acknowledgement and any reference already supplied.
suggestions.why: This helps connect later evidence to the existing report.
suggestions.action: Keep a copy of what you submitted. Log what you handed over and when. Ask the authority how it wants to receive additions.

suggestions.title: Footage from an authorised keeper
suggestions.look_for: If cameras cover the relevant place, note their owner and the narrow time window from your timeline.
suggestions.why: It may show movement or timing. A camera can have blind spots or an inaccurate clock.
suggestions.action: Ask the owner or investigating officer to preserve the original recording promptly. Record your request. Use only footage you are authorised to access.

suggestions.title: Witness position and changes at the scene
suggestions.look_for: Note where you and each witness stood, lighting, what was visible, and what changed before help arrived.
suggestions.why: It helps separate direct observations from later accounts and shows where a witness had a limited view.
suggestions.action: Let each person describe what they noticed independently. Share witness contact details privately with the authorities and only with permission where appropriate.

suggestions.title: Injury and professional records
suggestions.look_for: If anyone was injured, keep relevant treatment records when available and note when you first noticed the injury.
suggestions.why: An independent record can help establish timing and document what was treated.
suggestions.action: Get medical care first. Tell police about objects or marks that may be relevant and leave physical collection to them.

suggestions.title: Original records and an evidence log
suggestions.look_for: Keep records you lawfully have, with their surrounding context. For each item note the related event, who provided it, when you received it, and any transfer.
suggestions.why: The log distinguishes what you observed from what someone later told you and makes it easier to check the source.
suggestions.action: Keep an unchanged original and label working copies. Avoid editing originals, guessing gaps, or sharing evidence publicly.

next_steps: Take the confirmed timeline and evidence list to an appropriate legal professional.
